# Dr. Stuart Ryder

Image: Dr. Stuart Ryder

#### 

Veterinarian, Medical Director

Dr Ryder offers veterinary care including cancer chemotherapy for pets in Blue Springs and surrounding Kansas City areas.

As the Medial Director at Blue Springs Animal Hospital & Pet Resort, Dr. Ryder provides leadership for the doctor team and mentors new associate doctors.

Dr. Ryder received his Bachelor's Degree in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology  from  Oklahoma State University. He moved to the Kansas City area and joined the team at Blue Springs Animal Hospital in June of 2005 after he graduated with his Doctorate Degree in Veterinary Medicine from the North Carolina State University College of Veterinary Medicine. He grew up in Arkansas, and his wife Amanda grew up in Oklahoma, so Blue Springs is much closer to family!

Dr. Ryder’s interests include internal medicine and veterinary ultrasound. He has completed advanced training courses in veterinary ultrasound and enjoys using ultrasound to diagnose internal abdominal conditions. Dr. Ryder is also interested in veterinary dentistry and cancer chemotherapy . Dr. Ryder is happy to accept second opinions or local referrals for veterinary ultrasound, ultrasound-guided aspirates or biopsies of abdominal organs, and for cancer chemotherapy.

Dr. Ryder met his wife when they were attending Oklahoma State University for undergrad. She is a chemist and works with developing new pharmaceuticals. They have 3 four-legged children (2 cats and 1 dog), and 2 two-legged children, Michael and Savannah. Keeping track of everybody can be hard at times, so Dr. Ryder has recently acquired a taste for Starbucks!

When he is not at work, Dr. Ryder enjoys reading, camping, and running.

> It is a great blessing to come to work and really enjoy it.  Ever since I was in grade school, I wanted to be a veterinarian.  Damian Peyton came to the rescue, releasing 2.5 feet of gold thread that our tortie had eaten. To the doctors and staff, this all may just be in a days work. To us, they saved our family, treated our family, and sat with our family as we let one of our own go.

I can never truly repay anyone for the genuine kindness and care they have provided, other than tell everyone what wonderful pet people are working at BSAH. You all forever hold a place in our hearts, because you held once a piece of our hearts in your arms.

Image: JenniferK_Customer_Review_Cancer_Chemotherapy_Kansas_City-cat

* * *

Dr. Ryder is incredibly compassionate and understanding. I completely trust him with taking care of our beloved pets, who are as much family as pet. He is knowledgeable and goes the extra mile. I would highly recommend him as well as the entire staff of Blue Springs Animal Hospital.

* * *

If you’re searching for chemo treatment options for your pup, Blue Springs Animal Hospital is a great option! We went to Dr. We made the mistake of trying a local vet because they were closer,but we quickly learned that was a bad idea and switched back to BSAH. We usually switch between Dr. Peyton and Dr. Ryder and they're both amazing! The staff is amazing and are always so friendly and patient when our fur babies don't always want to cooperate and decide to be stubborn. We have 3 dogs now and I can honestly say that there's nowhere else I would rather take my pets to and we will continue to use them in the future and as long as we have pets. The level of care they give your pets is superior to anywhere else I've ever taken my previous pets. Not only do they get to know your pets,they take the time to get to know you as well and never hesitate to answer any questions or address any concerns you might have and they never rush you! Even if it's a little bit of a drive for you..take it! You won't regret it!

* * *

I had a senior cat with a lot of health problems. We had Dr. Ryder on speed dial!! He is a very attentive doctor and spends enough time as you need talking.

## What is a board-certified veterinary oncologist?

A board-certified veterinary oncologist is a veterinarian who has completed advanced, specialized training in oncology, the study and treatment of cancer in animals, after graduating from veterinary school.

This training typically includes three to five years of focused education, beginning with a rotating internship across medical and surgical specialties, followed by a residency dedicated specifically to cancer care. During this time, oncologists gain in-depth expertise in cancer diagnosis, treatment planning, chemotherapy, and compassionate long-term management.

To achieve board certification, veterinary oncologists must pass rigorous examinations and meet publication and training requirements set by the American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine (ACVIM). Veterinarians who complete all requirements earn Diplomate status, which signifies recognized board-certified specialty care in Medical Oncology.

Bachelor of Science in Biology. She worked for three years as an ICU nurse at Angell Memorial Animal Hospital in Boston

Veterinary Specialists in New York City. In 2010 she completed a three year residency in Small Animal Internal Medicine at
the University of Minnesota, which was sponsored by VCA. Dr. Carney has interests in all aspects of internal medicine,
particularly immune-mediated diseases, gastroenterology and endocrinology.

## Veterinary Oncology in the Front Range | MOVES Welcomes Dr. Jennifer J. Arthur, DVM, DACVR (RO)

  * February 2, 2026

MOVES is proud to introduce mobile veterinary oncology services in Colorado’s Front Range with the addition of Jennifer J. Arthur, DVM, DACVR (RO). As the first oncology specialist in this market for MOVES, Dr. Arthur brings a new level of advanced cancer care directly to a select group of partner hospitals across the region.

Dr. Arthur’s path to oncology is both unique and deeply rooted in a lifelong passion for animals. Originally earning a degree in English from Gettysburg College, she later pursued additional studies in Biology and Genetics at Colorado State University before going on to earn her Doctor of Veterinary Medicine from Ross University, completing her clinical training at Texas A&M.

Her advanced training includes a rotating internship at Kansas State University, a Radiation Oncology residency at North Carolina State University, and board certification through the American College of Veterinary Radiology (Radiation Oncology).
